title: Bus accidents in 1935 and 1936
summary: Wilson tells of two bus crashes, the first killing Cecil Irwin and the second sending the bus down an embankment.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Since that was a location job, some of the big bands, the leader sort of kept his distance from the other guys, you know. From what you've said, it doesn't seem to be the case with Earl. Was he -- well, when you were
Yeah, everybody traveled together. He traveled on the bus with us.
When did those accidents happen?

I'm trying to think when the first accident happened. I forgot the year. I think it was '35. We was in Iowa, traveling from Des Moines, Iowa to Minneapolis, open a theater engagement. You know, back in them days, a two-lane highway was real narrow. And one of those specially built trucks -- they had a flatbed truck and he had made it two-by-fours going across it like that, and sized that wide, to haul grain, you know, the farmers. And one of the corners of that body of that truck sideswiped just behind the bus driver. Just ripped that whole left side out. That's how Cecil Irwin got killed. Knocked him all the way back there, back with me.

The next accident was in '36. That was in the Cumberland Mountains. I don't know where we was going. We must have just left Baltimore, somewhere. Anyway, your road turned, and the bus driver didn't. He was after -- there was a loose bottle rolling up and down the aisle, and he turned around to tell somebody to pick up the bottle, and the road turned and he just kept going straight, and we went right down a 15-foot embankment. We landed at the bottom, end of the creek, and all

of that dust and running water, and reflection of the red lights from the bus on that dust, somebody hollared fire. And that did it. Me and Bish got hung up in the door upside down. The trumpet player, I don't know how the heck he got out, because you know, them buses had them windows that had the bars. I don't know how he got out, because when we got up to the top of the hill, up the road, he was standing up there waiting on us. I don't know how he got out of the bus. He got out that window some kind of way.
Was anybody hurt in that --

Yeah, Mitch-Bishop sprained his ankle. I think it was either sprained, or broke it. Anyway, he had trouble with it a long time. And a few minor injuries. The biggest one was when Franklin got his arm almost tore off and Cecil got killed.
That's still happening on the road, you know, the guys --
Oh, yeah.
It's always going to happen. Were you on your way to a gig when the accidents happened?
Uh-huh.
What -- you just cancelled the gig, or --
No, we played them. Show must go on.
Must have been tough, particularly
Without Cecil, yeah.
Had to go on and play after --
Uh-huh.
After Cecil'd been killed?
Yeah, then came home right after that. We filled out the engagements. Just what -- you know.
Must have been pretty rough traveling (inaudible).
